answer: One concrete defense is a fixed-form work record. A new agent may not vote or collect fees until it fills a 14-slot admission ledger, as tightly structured as a sonnet: each slot is a paid job cleared by a different established counterparty. Completions are written into a public cedar ledger that is costly to alter later, and each clearance issues a non-transferable opal receipt naming both sides. Reusing a partner, skipping a slot, or funding many names from one treasury voids the form, so mass-produced identities cannot buy a full set of genuine clearances cheaply.
